Prompt: Build a Native Lenovo LOQ Control Center for Windows

You are an expert Windows desktop and hardware-software integration engineer. Build a professional native Windows application for Lenovo LOQ laptops that monitors system health and controls Lenovo-supported performance/fan modes where the hardware interface is verified.

The application must prioritize hardware safety, truthful capability reporting, stability, and maintainability over exposing unsupported controls.

Project goal

Create a polished Windows 10/11 x64 desktop application named LOQ Control with a premium dark interface similar in quality to Lenovo Vantage, Armoury Crate, or MSI Center, but cleaner and lighter.

The application must support:

• CPU temperature and utilization monitoring
• GPU temperature and utilization monitoring
• CPU/GPU clock monitoring
• Fan RPM monitoring when genuinely available
• Lenovo firmware performance/power-mode switching when verified
• Manual fan speed or fan-curve control only when safely verified for the exact hardware
• Quiet, Balanced, Performance, and Custom profiles
• Automatic profile switching
• Windows startup
• System tray operation
• Hardware diagnostics
• Structured logging
• Safe fallback when hardware control is unavailable
• Hardware-independent automated tests

Never display fake sensor values or pretend that a command succeeded.

────────────────────

Critical hardware-safety requirements

Before implementing any hardware control, inspect and verify the actual interfaces available on the target machine.

Use only safe, bounded, documented or specifically verified interfaces.

Do not:

• Write arbitrary Embedded Controller registers
• Write undocumented ACPI addresses
• Use kernel memory manipulation
• Download random drivers
• Execute unsigned binaries
• Disable driver-signing enforcement
• Modify BIOS firmware
• Disable Lenovo, CPU, GPU, or Windows thermal protection
• Scan arbitrary command values such as every possible byte/value
• Treat Windows power-plan changes as direct fan-speed control
• Expose dangerous EC register editing to users

The application must never claim to control fan speed unless the requested operation is accepted and verified by the hardware interface.

If the interface only supports Lenovo preset modes, expose only those preset modes and clearly label direct RPM/fan-curve control as unavailable.

────────────────────

Required first step: inspect and verify the real interface

Before writing production fan-control code, execute safe read-only diagnostics in PowerShell.

Inspect:

Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\wmi -ClassName LENOVO_GAMEZONE_DATA
Get-CimClass -Namespace root\wmi -ClassName LENOVO_GAMEZONE_DATA
Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\wmi -ClassName LENOVO_FAN_METHOD
Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\wmi -ClassName LENOVO_FAN_TABLE_DATA
Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\wmi -ClassName LENOVO_FAN_MAX_SPEED_DATA
Get-CimClass -Namespace root\wmi -ClassName LENOVO_FAN_METHOD
Get-CimClass -Namespace root\wmi -ClassName LENOVO_FAN_TABLE_DATA
Get-CimClass -Namespace root\wmi -ClassName LENOVO_FAN_MAX_SPEED_DATA
Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\wmi -ClassName Lenovo_MachineInformation
Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\wmi -ClassName Lenovo_ACPI_Compliant_Virtual_Power_Controller

Also inspect whether the Lenovo device exists:

Test-Path '\\.\EnergyDrv'
Get-PnpDevice | Where-Object {
    $_.FriendlyName -match 'Lenovo|Energy|ACPI'
}

Read the current mode before changing anything.

If a mode-changing interface is discovered, use only known documented or previously verified preset values. For every command:

1. Read the current mode.
2. Save the original value.
3. Apply one known preset.
4. Read the mode back.
5. Confirm whether it changed.
6. Restore the original value.
7. Report the exact result.

Do not perform arbitrary value scans.

If a command changes only a Lenovo firmware performance mode and not fan RPM, name it accordingly. Do not call it manual fan control.

────────────────────

Technology requirements

Use:

• C#
• .NET 8 or newer LTS
• WPF or WinUI 3
• MVVM
• x64 target
• Nullable reference types enabled
• Dependency injection where useful
• Async and cancellable hardware polling
• No unnecessary third-party runtime dependencies

Preferred architecture:

Presentation
    ↓
Application
    ↓
Domain/Core
    ↓
Infrastructure
    ↓
Hardware Abstraction Layer
    ↓
Verified Lenovo/Windows Interface

Recommended structure:

LenovoLoqControl/
├── App/
├── UI/
│   ├── Views/
│   ├── ViewModels/
│   ├── Components/
│   └── Themes/
├── Core/
│   ├── HardwareManager/
│   ├── FanController/
│   ├── ThermalMonitor/
│   ├── ProfileManager/
│   ├── SafetyManager/
│   ├── Diagnostics/
│   └── Logging/
├── Hardware/
│   ├── Lenovo/
│   ├── EnergyDrv/
│   ├── Wmi/
│   ├── Acpi/
│   └── Sensors/
├── Services/
│   ├── StartupService/
│   ├── TrayService/
│   ├── NotificationService/
│   └── ProfileService/
├── Tests/
└── Installer/

Hardware code must be isolated from UI code.

────────────────────

Hardware abstraction layer

Define interfaces similar to:

public interface IHardwareMonitor
{
    HardwareIdentity Identity { get; }

    Task<SensorReading> ReadAsync(
        CancellationToken cancellationToken);
}

public interface IFanController
{
    bool IsSupported { get; }

    string AvailabilityMessage { get; }

    IReadOnlyCollection<FanMode> SupportedModes { get; }

    Task<FanControlResult> SetFanModeAsync(
        FanMode mode,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken);

    Task<FanControlResult> SetFanCurveAsync(
        FanCurve curve,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken);

    Task RestoreSafeStateAsync(
        CancellationToken cancellationToken);
}

Use nullable values for unavailable sensors:

public sealed record SensorReading(
    double? CpuTemperature,
    double? GpuTemperature,
    double? CpuUsage,
    double? GpuUsage,
    double? CpuClock,
    double? GpuClock,
    double? CpuFanRpm,
    double? GpuFanRpm,
    double? MemoryUsage,
    double? BatteryPercent,
    bool? IsCharging,
    DateTimeOffset Timestamp);

Every hardware operation must have:

• Timeout
• Cancellation
• Input validation
• Logging
• Explicit failure result
• Safe fallback
• No broad silent exception handling

Hardware polling must be rate-limited and must not continuously spam EC, ACPI, WMI, or device commands.

────────────────────

Lenovo hardware backend

Implement model-aware backend selection.

Detect:

• Manufacturer
• Product name
• Machine type
• BIOS version
• EC version if safely available
• Processor
• GPU
• Windows version
• Installed Lenovo hardware providers

Support different backends:

UnsupportedBackend
ReadOnlyMonitoringBackend
LenovoEnergyDrvBackend
LenovoVerifiedWmiBackend

The default behavior must be conservative.

EnergyDrv backend

If  \\.\EnergyDrv  is present and the capability probe succeeds:

• Expose only verified Lenovo firmware preset modes.
• Use strict allowlists for command values.
• Verify command completion by reading back state where possible.
• Serialize commands.
• Enforce a minimum delay between commands.
• Apply operation timeouts.
• Restore the original or safe Automatic mode on exit where technically possible.
• Never expose arbitrary IOCTL values to the UI.

If the device cannot be opened or the probe fails:

Fan/performance control unavailable
Monitoring remains available

Undocumented WMI interfaces

Do not enable undocumented WMI write methods by default.

If  LENOVO_GAMEZONE_DATA  or similar providers are present:

• They may be inspected read-only for diagnostics.
• Do not invoke  SetSmartFanMode  or equivalent methods unless the exact model, BIOS version, payload, and readback behavior have been verified and documented in code.
• Do not scan arbitrary values.
• Do not label undocumented methods as universally supported.

────────────────────

Core profiles

Implement:

Quiet

For:

• Browsing
• Documents
• Video playback
• Low noise

Balanced

For general use.

Performance

For:

• Gaming
• Compilation
• Rendering
• Heavy workloads

Custom

For user-defined settings only where supported.

Each profile should contain:

Name
Description
FanMode
FanCurve
CpuPolicy
GpuPolicy
TemperatureTargets
AutoSwitchRules

Support:

• Create
• Rename
• Duplicate
• Delete
• Import
• Export
• Save
• Restore
• Remember last profile

Do not make a profile appear to control a fan curve if the hardware backend does not support fan curves.

────────────────────

Fan curve validation

Implement and test a validator that rejects:

• Fewer than two points
• Temperatures outside the safe range
• Fan percentages outside 0–100
• Non-monotonic fan output
• Insufficient cooling at high temperatures
• Missing full cooling at critical temperatures
• Duplicate or invalid points
• Unsupported hardware curve ranges

Example safe curve:

45°C → 20%
55°C → 30%
65°C → 45%
75°C → 65%
85°C → 80%
95°C → 100%

If fan curves are unsupported, show the editor in a disabled state with a clear explanation.

────────────────────

Thermal safety

Implement:

Below 60°C       Cool
60–75°C           Normal
75–85°C           Warm
85–95°C           Hot
95°C and above   Critical

Thresholds must be configurable.

On critical temperature:

1. Request the safest supported cooling/performance mode.
2. Show a throttled Windows notification.
3. Log the event.
4. Apply the configured fallback profile.
5. Never disable firmware thermal protection.
6. Never claim that the application can prevent thermal shutdown.

Use notification deduplication to avoid spam.

────────────────────

User interface

Create a premium dark UI using:

Background: #0D0F12
Panels:     #12151A / #181C22
Accent:     #E2231A
Text:       #F4F6F8
Muted:      #8C96A5
Success:    #50D890

Use:

• Rounded cards
• Subtle gradients
• Good whitespace
• Strong typography
• Smooth transitions
• Responsive layout
• Keyboard accessibility
• 100%, 125%, and 150% scaling support
• 1080p, 1440p, and 4K layouts

Reusable components:

TemperatureCard
UsageCard
FanCard
ProfileSelector
TemperatureGraph
FanCurveEditor
SystemStatus
HardwareCompatibilityCard
SettingRow
Toggle
Slider
NotificationBanner

────────────────────

Dashboard

Display:

LENOVO LOQ
Model: LOQ 15IRX9
● System Healthy

Cards:

CPU
62°C
48% Usage
4.1 GHz

GPU
58°C
72% Usage
2.1 GHz

CPU FAN
3200 RPM

GPU FAN
2900 RPM

For unavailable values, show:

Unavailable

or:

Fan RPM unavailable

Never use fake or estimated values.

Show current mode:

Quiet
Balanced
Performance
Custom

If only firmware presets are supported, label the control:

Lenovo firmware performance mode

rather than:

Manual fan speed

────────────────────

Fan-control page

Show:

• Current CPU/GPU fan RPM when available
• Current Lenovo firmware mode
• Supported preset modes
• Hardware capability explanation
• Apply result
• Last command timestamp
• Failure details if rejected

Supported preset controls may include:

Automatic
Quiet/Silent
Balanced
Performance

Only expose  Max Cooling  if the exact backend supports and verifies it.

For unsupported features, display:

Custom fan curves are unavailable through the verified interface on this system.

Do not create fake sliders that only change local UI state.

────────────────────

Monitoring

Monitor efficiently:

• CPU temperature
• GPU temperature
• CPU utilization
• GPU utilization
• CPU clock
• GPU clock
• RAM usage
• Fan RPM
• Battery
• Charging state
• Power mode
• CPU/GPU power when available

Use configurable intervals with safe defaults.

Suggested defaults:

Hardware refresh: 2–3 seconds
Graph refresh: 1 second

All polling must be asynchronous and cancellable.

Graphs should support:

30 seconds
1 minute
5 minutes
15 minutes
30 minutes

────────────────────

Automatic profile switching

Support rules such as:

CPU > 75°C
→ Performance

CPU < 60°C for 2 minutes
→ Balanced

Cyberpunk2077.exe starts
→ Performance

Game exits
→ Balanced

Rules must include hysteresis/debounce to prevent rapid profile oscillation.

────────────────────

System tray

When minimized, support a Windows tray icon with:

LOQ Control

CPU: 62°C
GPU: 58°C
Mode: Performance

Quiet
Balanced
Performance
Custom

Open Dashboard
Settings
Exit

Do not create a permanent background service unless required.

────────────────────

Startup

Support:

• Start with Windows
• Start minimized
• Remember last profile

Use the Windows startup mechanism appropriate for a per-user application.

Do not require administrator privileges unless a specific verified hardware driver requires it. Explain any privilege requirement clearly.

────────────────────

Settings

Implement:

General

• Start with Windows
• Start minimized
• Theme
• Language
• Notifications

Monitoring

• Sensor refresh rate
• Graph refresh rate
• Temperature units
• Individual sensor enable/disable

Fan Control

• Default profile
• Safe fallback profile
• Hardware-control availability
• Curve settings

Advanced

• Hardware diagnostics
• Driver status
• Interface status
• Logging
• Debug mode

Never expose raw EC registers.

────────────────────

Diagnostics

Create a diagnostics page showing capability status:

Hardware Compatibility

✓ Lenovo laptop detected
✓ LOQ model detected
✓ CPU utilization
⚠ CPU temperature unavailable
⚠ GPU temperature unavailable
⚠ Fan RPM unavailable
✓ Lenovo firmware preset modes
⚠ Manual fan curves unavailable

Include:

Export Diagnostic Report

The report may contain:

• Manufacturer
• Product model
• Machine type
• BIOS version
• Windows version
• CPU/GPU names
• Detected interfaces
• Capability results
• Error codes
• Application version

Do not collect unnecessary personal information.

────────────────────

Logging

Implement structured logs such as:

[10:32:14] Hardware initialized
[10:32:15] Lenovo model detected: LOQ 15IRX9
[10:32:15] CPU temperature unavailable
[10:32:20] Profile changed: Balanced -> Performance
[10:32:20] Lenovo firmware mode request accepted

Never log secrets, personal files, usernames, or unrelated system information.

────────────────────

Installer

Create a professional installer that:

• Installs the application
• Creates a Start Menu shortcut
• Optionally creates a desktop shortcut
• Registers startup behavior
• Supports upgrades
• Supports clean uninstall
• Does not install unnecessary services or drivers

Do not bundle unsigned kernel drivers.

────────────────────

Tests

Create unit and integration-style hardware-independent tests for:

• Fan curve validation
• Thermal classification
• Profile switching
• Auto-switch hysteresis
• Configuration loading
• Configuration saving
• Import/export
• Unsupported hardware behavior
• Mode allowlisting
• Command rate limiting
• Timeout handling
• Safe restoration behavior
• Diagnostic report generation

Use mocked hardware interfaces. Tests must run without a Lenovo laptop.

────────────────────

Development process

Work in this order:

1. Inspect the existing repository.
2. Inspect and verify actual Lenovo interfaces.
3. Record the exact verified hardware behavior.
4. Define the hardware abstraction layer.
5. Implement read-only monitoring.
6. Implement safe Lenovo firmware preset control if verified.
7. Implement the core application services.
8. Implement profiles.
9. Implement UI and dashboard.
10. Implement diagnostics and logging.
11. Implement tray and startup.
12. Implement installer.
13. Add automated tests.
14. Run build, tests, and smoke tests.
15. Perform a security and stability review.

Do not leave core functionality as TODO placeholders.

If a requested feature cannot be safely verified, implement the monitoring and diagnostics behavior, clearly mark the feature unavailable, and document why.

────────────────────

Acceptance criteria

The application is complete only when:

• It builds successfully for Windows x64.
• Automated tests pass.
• The GUI launches without crashing.
• Missing sensors do not crash the app.
• Unsupported controls are visibly disabled or unavailable.
• No fake fan RPM or temperature values are displayed.
• No arbitrary EC/ACPI/kernel writes exist.
• Lenovo preset commands are strictly allowlisted.
• Every accepted control command is read back or otherwise verified.
• Original/safe mode restoration is attempted on exit.
• Hardware polling is cancellable and rate-limited.
• Diagnostics clearly explain available and unavailable capabilities.
• The README documents the tested Lenovo interfaces and limitations.
• A real Lenovo LOQ test procedure is documented.
• The application never claims direct fan control unless direct fan control is genuinely verified

This is the project
